full_inspection: I inspected all four complete native halves of sites026 and102, including the body, displayed symbols, footnote, margins and foliation, and the enlarged copy2 deletion detail. Every original line, note, macro and D2 row was compared; all observed differing loci and the shared hand call are recorded below.
original_transcription_comparison: The supplied originals differ in the copy2 deletion and margin x, footnote punctuation reading, archive foliation and metadata. Both originally chose trouve and left a bare newline after géométrico-. The scans show the shared right-open word glyph and the same printed hyphen; both checked copies now carry recorded syntax-only percent repairs.

entries.decision: restore the shared explicit word doubt in copy2
entries.reason: Both impressions show the same right-open third letter. The copy2 source had silently selected trouve.

entries.decision: record the matching syntax-only repairs, preserving the printed hyphen
entries.reason: Both original sources used a bare newline after the same printed hyphen. Recorded mechanical transitions now add percent in both checked copies to suppress the spurious TeX interword space; the observed hyphen and letters are unchanged.

entries.decision: retain the shared elevated note call
entries.reason: A small handwritten (5) stands after ici before the typed period in each copy. Similar placement does not establish authorship.

entries.decision: retain the copy1 punctuation doubt and the clear copy2 period
entries.reason: Copy1 has two vertically separated dark points at this position; copy2 has a single baseline period. The original doubt about the additional copy1 point is retained.

entries.decision: retain the two-position deletion with doubtful covered letters
entries.reason: Oblique hatching crosses the positions occupied by at in copy1. The remaining ink supports that reading but does not expose both full letters.
A small handwritten x is visible in the left margin beside the footnote line containing the deletion.
The lower-left margins show hand26 and hand102 respectively; no attribution of this foliation handwriting is made.
